newsitem.title: QATAR: Portillo offers Qatar Gulf security proposal.
newsitem.headline: Portillo offers Qatar Gulf security proposal.

text.p: British Defence Secretary Michael Portillo said on Monday he had offered a comprehensive Gulf security proposal to Qatar.

"We offered a security proposal to Qatar because it is clear that Qatar is trying to play a full part in the security of this region," Portillo said. He did not disclose any details of the proposal or how it would function.

"Britain remains very much interested in security and defence matters in the Gulf and Qatar is expected to play an important role," he told reporters at the end of a two-day visit to the state, a small peninsula east of Saudi Arabia.
Diplomats said Portillo's offer was part of a British bid to find a fresh foothold in lower Gulf states from where it voluntarily withdrew in 1970.
They said the talks also focused on Britain's bid to sell 50 main battle tanks to Qatar's 8,000-strong army in competition with similar efforts by France and the United States.

All three Western powers have defence treaties with Qatar, whose hydrocarbon reserves -- the third largest in the world after Russia's and Iran's -- make it one of the most strategic sources of vital clean energy in the next century.

Portillo said he made the security proposal during his meetings with the Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani, Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Khalifa al-Thani and Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani.

Qatar will host the next annual summit of the Gulf Cooperation Council in December and hold the 1997 chairmanship of the political and economic bloc, which also groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates.
